statement: RH iff for every integer j>=3, there exists finite C_j>=0 and arbitrarily large integers m such that G(n)<=C_j*n^theta_j at every integer node n of the grid for theta_j=1/2+1/j on [m^2,m^3].
proof: RH => G(x)=O(sqrt(x)) from source explicit formula, so yes. Converse: for each j, exact grid h^(4j)<=8^(2j) a^(3j+2) ensures G(x)<=(C_j+1)x^theta_j for all real x in [m^2,m^3]. Given any tau>1/2 choose j so theta_j<tau, then m large enough that (C_j+1)*(m^2)^(theta_j-tau)<=1. Thus G(x)<=x^tau on arbitrarily far-out [m^2,m^3]. Source one-sided Landau interval lemma implies no zeta zeros with Re>tau; take tau down to half and functional equation to deduce RH. No hidden extension to arbitrary leading constants required.
notes: This is strictly a conditional restatement and not a proof, since it supplies no uniform C_j or arithmetic G values for arbitrarily large m. It reduces quantifiers to countable j and integer grid nodes but still an infinite unproved arithmetic condition. Source Part II sections 4-5 are pointwise in x and permits auxiliary q,d to vary with x; a weakened H12 need only establish pointwise hypotheses at those nodes WITH constants uniform in m and x. This does not follow from finite testing.
